explain.say: An electric heater turns each unit of electricity into one unit of heat. A heat pump does something cleverer: it uses electricity to move heat that already exists, from outside to inside.

explain.say: For each unit of electricity running the compressor, a typical heat pump delivers about three units of heat into the house. Engineers call this ratio the coefficient of performance, and people often say 300 percent efficient.

faq.q: Does a heat pump break the laws of physics?
faq.a: No. Energy is not created: the electricity used plus the heat taken from outside equals the heat delivered inside. It only seems like more than 100 percent because the outside heat is free.

faq.q: Where does the extra heat come from?
faq.a: From the outdoor air, the ground or water, which are warmed by the sun. A heat pump gathers that low-temperature heat and concentrates it at a useful temperature.
asks: Where does a heat pump get its heat?

faq.q: What is the coefficient of performance?
faq.a: It is the heat delivered divided by the electricity used. A coefficient of performance of 3 means 3 kilowatt-hours of heat for every kilowatt-hour of electricity, and good systems average about 3 or more over a year.

faq.q: Why are heat pumps less efficient in very cold weather?
faq.a: When it is colder outside, the heat must be lifted across a bigger temperature gap, so the compressor works harder for each unit of heat. Modern heat pumps still work well below freezing.
asks: Do heat pumps work in the cold?

faq.q: Is a heat pump cheaper to run than a gas boiler?
faq.a: It depends on prices. A heat pump uses roughly a third as much energy as a boiler for the same heat, but electricity usually costs more per kilowatt-hour than gas, so the savings vary.

facts: A heat pump with a coefficient of performance of 3 delivers 3 kilowatt-hours of heat for each kilowatt-hour of electricity.
Energy is conserved in a heat pump: the heat delivered equals the electricity used plus the heat taken from outside.

quiz.say: A heat pump uses 2 kilowatt-hours of electricity and delivers 6 kilowatt-hours of heat. What is its coefficient of performance?
quiz.show: COP with 2 kWh in and 6 kWh of heat out?
quiz.why: The coefficient of performance is heat out divided by electricity in: 6 divided by 2 is 3.
